headline: Asia Cup: Tigresses face do-or-die UAE clash for semifinal spot
summary: Bangladesh Women's team must win their final Group B match to keep their campaign alive and advance to the semifinals.
details: The Bangladesh Women's cricket team faces a critical encounter against the UAE on Tuesday in their final Group B fixture of the Women's Asia Cup.
A victory is essential for the Tigresses, as a defeat will result in their elimination from the tournament.
Bangladesh previously won their opening match against Thailand by 71 runs, but suffered a loss to Sri Lanka after their batting unit failed to score a high total.
Despite the batting struggles, pacer Marufa Akter stood out in the last match, claiming three wickets for 21 runs.
Batter Sobhana Mostary noted that the team is focusing on improving their batting and fielding to ensure a win against the UAE.
The team will rely on pace spearhead Marufa Akter and skipper Nigar Sultana Joty to lead the way in this decisive match.
caption:
Win or go home. The Tigresses are fighting for a semifinal berth in a high-stakes clash against the UAE.

The Bangladesh Women's cricket team faces a critical encounter against the UAE on Tuesday in their final Group B fixture of the Women's Asia Cup.

A victory is essential for the Tigresses, as a defeat will result in their elimination from the tournament.

Bangladesh previously won their opening match against Thailand by 71 runs, but suffered a loss to Sri Lanka after their batting unit failed to score a high total.

Despite the batting struggles, pacer Marufa Akter stood out in the last match, claiming three wickets for 21 runs.

Batter Sobhana Mostary noted that the team is focusing on improving their batting and fielding to ensure a win against the UAE.

The team will rely on pace spearhead Marufa Akter and skipper Nigar Sultana Joty to lead the way in this decisive match.

headline_marked: Two more accused [[placed on 3-day remand]] in DMCH doctor assault case
headline: Two more accused placed on 3-day remand in DMCH doctor assault case
summary: The suspects were remanded following the attack on Professor Asadur Rahman, who was allegedly targeted after refusing a $15,000 extortion demand.
details: A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate's court has granted a three-day remand for two more suspects, Sabbir Hossain (18) and Fahim Ishraq Labib (20), in connection with the assault on a senior doctor.
caption:
A senior DMCH doctor was assaulted after refusing a $15,000 extortion demand. Two more suspects are now on remand.

A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate's court has granted a three-day remand for two more suspects, Sabbir Hossain (18) and Fahim Ishraq Labib (20), in connection with the assault on a senior doctor.
